```{r}
# --- Chunk 2: Read & clean the first data set
# (Equivalent to pd.read_csv('ovd_EBOE.csv', sep=';') and drop_duplicates in Python)

df <- read_csv2("ovd_EBOE.csv") %>%  # read_csv2 uses semicolon as default sep
  distinct()                         # remove duplicates

# Rename columns: T_BITA_COB_DT -> cob_dt, AMT -> AMT, CCY_CUST_PRINC -> cur
df <- df %>%
  rename(
    cob_dt = T_BITA_COB_DT,
    AMT    = AMT,
    cur    = CCY_CUST_PRINC
  )

# Convert date columns to Date; adjust format if needed
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    cob_dt     = as.Date(cob_dt, format="%Y-%m-%d"),
    DT_ACC_OPN = as.Date(DT_ACC_OPN, format="%Y-%m-%d")
  )

# If "AMT" has commas, replace with dots & convert to numeric
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    AMT = gsub(",", ".", AMT),
    AMT = as.numeric(AMT)
  )

# Create "first_dt_on" = earliest cob_dt for each GID_CONT
dfint <- df %>%
  group_by(GID_CONT) %>%
  summarise(first_dt_on = min(cob_dt, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Merge first_dt_on back to df
df <- df %>%
  left_join(dfint, by="GID_CONT")

# Show a few rows (optional)
head(df)

```

```{r}
# --- Chunk 3: Read & filter the second data set
# (Equivalent to second pd.read_csv('4052_OVD_input.csv', sep=';'))

df <- read_csv2("4052_OVD_input.csv")

# Keep rows: MODEL_ID == '4052_NP_OVD' and FLG_NPE == 'N'
df <- df %>%
  filter(MODEL_ID == "4052_NP_OVD", FLG_NPE == "N")

# Show a few rows (optional)
head(df)

```

```{r}
# --- Chunk 4: Summarize & pivot wide
# Sort, group_by, sum, then pivot_wider (equivalent of pivot in Python)

df <- df %>%
  arrange(cob_dt, cur) %>%
  group_by(cur, cob_dt, T_BITA_TNT_CD, GID_CONT, DT_ACC_OPN, FLG_NPE, MODEL_ID, first_dt_on) %>%
  summarise(AMT = sum(AMT, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

df_wide <- df %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = c(cur, T_BITA_TNT_CD, GID_CONT, DT_ACC_OPN, FLG_NPE, MODEL_ID, first_dt_on),
    names_from  = cob_dt,
    values_from = AMT
  )

# Display the pivoted data (optional)
df_wide

```

```{r}
# --- Chunk 5: Create "df_prev_1" which is the same table but shifted by one column
df_prev_1 <- df_wide

col_names <- colnames(df_wide)
# Suppose the first 7 columns are ID cols, and the rest are date columns:
for(i in seq_along(col_names)) {
  if(i >= 8) {
    if(i == 8) {
      # first date column replaced with NA
      df_prev_1[[col_names[i]]] <- NA
    } else {
      # each subsequent date column replaced with the previous
      df_prev_1[[col_names[i]]] <- df_wide[[col_names[i - 1]]]
    }
  }
}

# Show a few rows (optional)
head(df_prev_1)

```

```{r}
# --- Chunk 6: Stack / unpivot both data frames into long form
df_long <- df_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(cur, T_BITA_TNT_CD, GID_CONT, DT_ACC_OPN, FLG_NPE, MODEL_ID, first_dt_on),
    names_to  = "cob_dt",
    values_to = "AMT"
  )

df_prev_1_l <- df_prev_1 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(cur, T_BITA_TNT_CD, GID_CONT, DT_ACC_OPN, FLG_NPE, MODEL_ID, first_dt_on),
    names_to  = "cob_dt",
    values_to = "AMT_prev"
  )

# Join them so that each row in df_long has a corresponding AMT_prev
df_long <- df_long %>%
  left_join(
    df_prev_1_l,
    by=c("cur","T_BITA_TNT_CD","GID_CONT","DT_ACC_OPN","FLG_NPE","MODEL_ID","first_dt_on","cob_dt")
  )

# Show a few rows (optional)
head(df_long)

```

```{r}
# --- Chunk 7: Compute changes & new columns (Change_EoM, etc.)
df_long <- df_long %>%
  mutate(
    Change_EoM    = coalesce(AMT, 0) - coalesce(AMT_prev, 0),
    AMT_INCREASED = if_else(Change_EoM >  0, Change_EoM, 0),
    AMT_DECREASED = if_else(Change_EoM <  0, Change_EoM, 0),
    AMT_NB        = if_else(cob_dt == first_dt_on, Change_EoM, 0),
    AMT_closed    = if_else(is.na(AMT) & AMT_prev > 0, AMT_prev, 0)
  )

head(df_long)

```

```{r}
# --- Chunk 8: Aggregate & final results
df_agg <- df_long %>%
  group_by(cur, cob_dt, MODEL_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    AMT            = sum(AMT, na.rm=TRUE),
    AMT_prev       = sum(AMT_prev, na.rm=TRUE),
    Change_EoM     = sum(Change_EoM, na.rm=TRUE),
    AMT_INCREASED  = sum(AMT_INCREASED, na.rm=TRUE),
    AMT_DECREASED  = sum(AMT_DECREASED, na.rm=TRUE),
    AMT_NB         = sum(AMT_NB, na.rm=TRUE),
    AMT_closed     = sum(AMT_closed, na.rm=TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(cur), desc(cob_dt)) %>%
  mutate(
    CheckChangeSum = AMT - AMT_prev
  )

# In Python, a final step zeroes out a few columns in row 0:
if(nrow(df_agg) > 0) {
  df_agg[1, c("Change_EoM", "AMT_INCREASED", "AMT_DECREASED", "CheckChangeSum")] <- 0
}

# Show final aggregated DataFrame
df_agg
```
